Nov 21 : Kylian Mbappe’s third miss in his last six penalty attempts for club and country did not prove costly as Carlos Espi’s late winner helped Real Madrid to a 2-1 home victory over Celta Vigo in LaLiga on Saturday. Real have 33 points from 13 LaLiga games, level with leaders Barcelona, but have now played a game more. The Catalans are in action on Sunday at home to Villarreal. Mbappe’s wastefulness from 12-yards had already cost Real a point earlier in the season and this time it was almost two as he lifted his effort well over the crossbar. He also missed a penalty when the Madrid side lost 1-0 at Real Betis in September, and for France against Morocco in the World Cup.

On both those occasions he shot low and saw his effort saved, which perhaps might explain why he tried to go high this time round. Celta took the lead inside six minutes when Pablo Duran scored from close range as he turned in Williot Swedberg's low cross. Real had the chance to pull level when Mbappe had his arm pulled by Celta defender Javier Rodriguez and the referee pointed to the spot, but the Frenchman could not convert. Real were level on 66 minutes as Jude Bellingham drilled the ball low into the net from just inside box. It looked as though they would be frustrated before Espi’s initial header was saved by goalkeeper Ionut Radu, but he turned in the rebound. Kike Salas equalised in added time at the end of the game as Sevilla played to a 1-1 draw with Real Betis in the Seville derby. Antony netted for the visitors early in the second half with his first goal of the season but Betis were denied a place in the top three by the equaliser. Deportivo Alaves ended an eight-game winless streak with a 3-1 home victory over Deportivo La Coruna. Angel Perez opened the scoring for the hosts, but they were pegged back to 1-1 by an own goal from Nahuel Tenaglia. Lucas Boye, who earlier missed a penalty, scored Alaves' second and the points were made safe when Denis Suarez netted in added time. Valencia moved out of the bottom three with a 1-0 away win at Rayo Vallecano thanks to Jose Copete's first half headed goal.

Source: Reuters

CARDIFF, Nov 21 : Australia brought Wales down to earth after last weekend's historic victory over the All Blacks with a narrow 29-26 Nations Championship win on Saturday that secured the Wallabies a spot in the fifth-place playoff. A packed Millennium Stadium crowd, still relishing the memory of a first win over New Zealand in 73 years, was in full voice throughout but silenced at fulltime as Wales fell to a seventh loss in 12 tests this year. Tries from Taniela Tupou and Brandon Paenga-Amosa gave Australia a 12-7 lead at halftime and Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau crossed after the break as the Wallabies snapped a four-match losing streak. The win sent Australia above Argentina into third place in the Southern Hemisphere standings and they will play Ireland at Twickenham next Friday.

"I'm stoked with it. Test match win after four losses on the trot," captain Harry Wilson said after leading Australia to their first win in Europe since they beat the Welsh in Cardiff two years ago. "We worked hard to get a win today against very strong team. I'm super happy with it. It gives us a lot of confidence going into next week, and we really want to finish strong." Wales finished fifth in the Northern Hemisphere standings and will play Japan in the playoff for ninth place in London on Saturday. "I think that's the highs and lows of the game we play, isn't it?" Wales captain Dewi Lake said. "Come off a major high last week, and you know didn't quite get it done today. But I think all credit to the Aussies ... I can't fault the effort the boys have put in again. Unfortunately, it wasn't to be today for us." The home side were held up over the line twice before hooker Lake scored two tries off the back of rolling mauls either side of halftime. BACKLINE SKILLS Wales showcased brilliant backline skills to send fullback Blair Murray over for a try in the 55th minute that briefly put them in front at 21-19. The Wallabies had an Allan Alaalatoa try scratched off for a knock-on around the hour mark but centre Ikitau went over in the 64th minute on the back of 24 attacking phases. Australia flyhalf Carter Gordon slotted a penalty in the 74th minute to give the Wallabies a 29-21 lead, which proved enough for victory despite Wales securing a fourth try through replacement hooker Ryan Elias two minutes from time. Wales battled for the winning score in the last few minutes but their attempt to go the length of the field was ended when the ball was knocked on.

Source: Reuters

PARIS, Nov 21 : France booked another showdown against world champions South Africa in the first Nations Championship final after securing a 45-17 bonus-point victory over Argentina at the Stade de France on Saturday. Mickael Guillard, Peato Mauvaka, Kalvin Gourgues (two), Emilien Gailleton, Tyler Duguid and Louis Bielle-Biarrey scored tries to earn the Six Nations champions clinch the attacking bonus point. Argentina, who have not won in France since 2014, scored tries through Justo Piccardo and Pablo Matera, with Tomas Albornoz kicking seven points. Les Bleus topped the Northern Hemisphere standings with 26 points, one point ahead of England, while Argentina sit fourth in the Southern Hemisphere table on 11 points.

"We got the job done, but we can't be too happy with what we did in the first half," Guillard told TF1. Following England's bonus-point victory over New Zealand, France took to the pitch knowing that only a bonus-point win would send them to the final next Sunday at Twickenham. They did it the hard way after a poor first half. After an emotional tribute to former Argentina rugby international Federico Aramburu, who was shot dead four years ago in Paris and whose son took to the pitch with both captains, France struck early through Guillard. Argentina, however, dominated most of the first half. They levelled 10 minutes later through Justo Piccardo and Felipe Contepomi's side moved ahead thanks to Albornoz's penalty. ARGENTINA REDUCED TO 13 MEN France's lack of discipline and turnovers prevented them from developing their passing game. Matthieu Jalibert, who was back at flyhalf after two months out, did not change much but France went into the break with a 14-10 lead, thanks to Mauvaka's try from a lineout maul. "We felt, during the first half, a France team that was doubting itself, hesitating and unable to let go," coach Fabien Galthie told TF1. "Going into the break at 14-10 was already a victory in itself." France showed better intent after halftime, with Gourgues breaking through the Argentine defence to score the third try. The fourth try finally came from substitute Gailleton in the right corner, while Argentina were playing with a man short after Mayco Vivas was shown a yellow card for a dangerous clear-out at a ruck. The Pumas were reduced to 13 men when captain Julian Montoya was sent to the sin bin. Vivas' card was upgraded to a 20-minute red by the bunker review system and Tyler Duguid and Gourgues took full advantage to score two quick tries. Matera claimed Argentina's consolation try, but Bielle-Biarrey replied for France six minutes later. Next Sunday's final will bring another clash against South Africa, after France stunned the four-times world champions eight days ago with a 21-19 victory. Argentina will face Scotland on Sunday.

Source: Reuters

FAST

DUBLIN, Nov 21 : Ireland coach Andy Farrell said the turnaround in his side's scrum from being decimated by South Africa last year to standing up in Saturday's 20-17 win epitomised the progress they are making towards next year's World Cup. The Springboks' overwhelming scrum pressure in Dublin almost exactly 12 months ago left a dazed Ireland playing part of that game with 12 men following a frenzy of yellow cards and lucky to escape with just a 24-13 defeat. Farrell described as "huge" the moment his pack turned the tables on 26 minutes on Saturday with a powerful shove that elicited a huge roar from the crowd and while South Africa were still a force at the setpiece, it was a much more even battle. "I think it epitomised what we were about in general," Farrell told a news conference, crediting his side for "just getting on with it" when any pack knows it's not always going to go their way against the world's best scrummagers.

Captain Dan Sheehan, playing at the back instead of the front of the scrum for only the second time in his professional career due to an injury crisis at number eight, said the real focus put into the scrum in recent months was paying off. "It's more a mentality of buying in. We can look at angles and all this crap, but if you don't go forward, you're not getting anywhere. It's as simple as that, really," he added when asked if the improvements were technical or mental. South Africa assistant coach Felix Jones, a former Ireland international, said that while the world champions still felt they were dominant in the scrum overall, there was no question Ireland had definitely improved in that area. Fellow assistant Mzwandile Stick, who was handling match day duties alongside Jones with Rassie Erasmus serving the first of a six-match ban, said the Springboks' discipline let them down and that their usually reliable kicking game was not where they wanted it to be. A losing bonus point means they have a Nations Championship final to make amends next week. For Farrell, whose side remain in contention for the third-place playoff, a win against a team that is "by a stretch" the world's best represented a big step forward. "That was the aim, to deliver when it matters and this game mattered to us. We didn't shy away from that and we were able to perform," he said. "I've said it already with the World Cup in 10 months' time, 11 months' time, it's all about stepping stones and this is a big one, that's for sure."

Source: Reuters

NEWCASTLE, England, Nov 21 : Arsenal dropped two points in a 2-2 Premier League draw at Newcastle United on Saturday, and that disappointment may be compounded if goalkeeper David Raya has to miss significant time after suffering an arm injury.  Raya left the field holding his left arm in the 70th minute and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. "Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news. He will get assessed now, and probably he will have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly, because at the moment, I don't know," Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta told reporters.  "It was a knock. I don't know how it happened and what the injury is at the moment, so we have to wait and see tomorrow."

HELSINKI: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday ( Nov 21) and later drifted into Finnish waters, prompting Helsinki to impose temporary air and maritime restrictions and say Ukraine was probably behind the attack. The Sparta II, bound for Russian exclave Kaliningrad , was damaged in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, Finland 's Defence Forces said, corroborating an earlier account by Russian officials. "It is likely that Ukraine...is behind (the attack)," Finnish armed forces spokesperson Aki-Mauri Huhtinen told a press conference, adding it was not clear why the vessel had been targeted. Finland 's Border Guard said there was no danger to maritime traffic or people, that rescue units were at the scene, and that it was coordinating operations with neighbouring countries.

Gulf of Finland coast guard commander Mikko Simola later told a press conference the vessel had anchored and its crew was evacuating. Helsinki said it had introduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland to protect civilians and allow authorities to operate if drones needed to be intercepted. "The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland , where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X. Ukraine's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Russia's embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The vessel is subject to US sanctions and is linked to Russian ship ping company Oboronlogistika, according to the US Treasury Department. Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian defence ministry, according to the company's website. "At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military materiel on board," Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin told Reuters. Helsinki said separately that a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating Finnish airspace on Saturday, possibly in connection with rescue or monitoring operations involving the damaged vessel.

RUSSIA SAYS DRONES SHOT DOWN OVER LENINGRAD REGION Leningrad region Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Telegram that a cargo vessel had been attacked by two drones in international waters about 3 nautical miles from Russia's border. He did not identify the vessel. Drozdenko also said 80 drones had been shot down over the Leningrad region overnight. Finland 's military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian war ship in the same area during a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks on the Leningrad region. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said on X his country was monitoring the situation and had offered assistance to Finland , without providing details. Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board said in an emailed statement that preliminary information indicated there had been explosions on board the Sparta II, and that it was also monitoring the situation. Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region. Kaliningrad , which lies between Poland and Lithuania, has periodically been a flashpoint between Russia and NATO and the European Union. Russia has previously described attacks on its commercial vessels outside its territorial waters as acts of terrorism and maritime piracy. The Sparta II is a 121-metre Russian-flagged cargo vessel owned by Oboronlogistika that left St Petersburg on Friday, according to LSEG data. The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia that extends east to St Petersburg. Gogland lies in the eastern Gulf of Finland , about 40 km from Finland 's coast.

Source: Reuters/fs

Nov 21 (Field Level Media) - Spain's most accomplished tennis star is now helping make decisions for one of the country's biggest soccer clubs. Rafael Nadal, who won 22 grand slam titles over a 23-year career, was approved to join the Real Madrid board of directors by a 99.5 per cent vote of the club's general member assembly Saturday. The 40-year-old becomes the 19th member of the board. "It is a great responsibility to be part of the Board of Directors of Real Madrid," Nadal said in a statement. "This club is passed down from parents to children and unites people. For me, it connects me with family and friends to watch matches together. It's an immense joy and a great satisfaction." The appointment is expected to be a victory for club president Florentino Perez, whose leadership has been the subject of recent criticism. The club has not won a trophy since 2024.

NEWCASTLE, England, Nov 21 : Arsenal missed the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League as they were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday, with Mikel Arteta's side having to fight back from 2-1 down after a spirited display from their hosts. Arsenal looked set for an easy evening in the first half and they took the lead in the 33rd minute, Eberechi Eze latching on to a superb angled pass from Kai Havertz to sweep the ball into the net. Booed off at the break, Newcastle levelled four minutes into the second half as Martin Odegaard was robbed from a throw-in by William Osula. The Danish striker fed the ball to Harvey Barnes, who took a touch before rifling the ball past the keeper. In the 62nd minute the home side went ahead, Malick Thiaw bundling the ball into the net from close range after Arsenal failed to clear a corner. Arsenal keeper David Raya then suffered an arm injury and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Nov 21 : Rassie Erasmus’ watch-along in South Africa’s 20-17 loss to Ireland on Saturday provided a range of emotions but not much in the way of insight from the Springbok coach, who is serving a six-match ban for criticising match officials. Erasmus hosted a live-stream of himself watching the game from the team’s Dublin hotel, and in the week had over 100,000 people request to view the match with him on a platform he had created. He was sat in what appeared to be a conference room, drinking diet coke and getting increasingly animated as the game went on. Erasmus celebrated his team’s two tries as you would expect him too, but largely sat sullen without much in the way of expression.

Under the terms of his suspension, he may not have direct or indirect contact with the team during matches. NICE, France, Nov 21 : Champions Paris St Germain fought back after conceding early at Nice on Saturday to win 3-2 and extend their Ligue 1 lead, but it came at a potentially heavy cost as France international Desire Doue injured his knee. PSG advanced to 26 points from 11 matches, moving further ahead of second-placed Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Olympique Lyonnais and stayed on 21 points. "We need to wait for tomorrow's medical examinations, but it is clearly a serious injury. We could see that on television,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said after a tearful Doue was stretchered off near the end of the first half. "I have spoken with him. We need to wait for the final medical examinations to know exactly what the injury is, but it is clearly a serious one."

Nice went ahead against PSG after eight minutes after winning possession high up the pitch, Mohamed Amoura finishing clinically with a low shot into the far corner. TWISTED AWKWARDLY Senny Mayulu equalised from a 31st-minute penalty, awarded for handball after a VAR review, and Doue netted within 60 seconds from Achraf Hakimi’s cross. Seven minutes later, however, Doue went down after twisting awkwardly as he tried to control the ball. His potential absence will be a major blow to the European champions who are already without influential playmaker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia due to a serious knee injury. Ousmane Dembele came on as a substitute to set up Ferran Torres to extend PSG’s lead in the 85th minute before Nice full back Ali Abdi pulled one back in stoppage time. Lille remained second despite their home setback with Mads Bodstrup scoring the game’s only goal for Lyon, who moved up to fourth in the standings on 20 points. Strasbourg, who changed their coach in midweek, also lost at home and slipped down to 15th as Brest beat them 1-0 in Vitor Matos’ debut in charge. Noah Edjouma punished a poor clearance to score after 22 minutes. Didier Digard’s first game in charge of RC Lens, struggling this season after being runners-up in the last campaign, ended 1-1 at home against Toulouse. Monaco have now gone six Ligue 1 matches without a win, but did score late to salvage a 1-1 home draw with Auxerre.  (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

DUBLIN, Nov 21 : Two first-half tries from Rob Baloucoune helped a rejuvenated Ireland beat South Africa 20-17 on Saturday but a losing bonus point was enough to book the world champions a place in next weekend's Nations Championship final. With Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus watching on from his hotel serving the first of a six-match ban, Ireland dominated the first period and led the subdued Springboks 17-10 at halftime thanks to Baloucoune's tries and one from Ronan Kelleher. A Sam Prendergast penalty stretched the lead to 10 points and while a Malcolm Marx try cut it to three just before the hour, the Springboks could not breach the excellent Irish defence and fell to back-to-back defeats. "It's some effort from the lads. It's never going to be perfect against the world's best but we kept getting back into the game when we've just had something that's disappointing," said Ireland coach Andy Farrell.

"It's just shows the character of the lads. It shows us where we're at 10 months out from a World Cup." Farrell's men, who began the day with an outside shot of topping the Northern Hemisphere standings, cannot catch England but are guaranteed a top-three finish and one of the marquee games at the November 27-29 finals weekend at Twickenham. ERASMUS WATCHES ON FROM AFAR The build-up was dominated by Erasmus' ban for questioning the integrity of match officials following last week's loss to France and while some visiting fans sported masks of their suspended coach, his players' performance offered little support. They had demolished the Ireland scrum when they won in Dublin a year ago and looked ready to pick up where they left off on Saturday with a couple of early easy shoves handing Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu the opportunity to put them 3-0 up. But Ireland were a different beast this time and roared straight back, stretching the visitors with Stuart McCloskey finding Baloucoune with a fine long pass for the winger to step smartly inside for the opening try of the game on eight minutes. The in-form Ulster man was almost in again shortly after, only to lose his grip on the ball at the last second but he only had to wait a couple more minutes to notch his fourth try of the competition. While a rare obliteration of the South Africa scrum brought the biggest roar of the game and celebrations among the Irish pack who competed far better throughout, it was the Springboks' steamrolling set-piece that set up Morne van den Berg to level the scores against the run of play four minutes from the break. However, the hosts took a deserved lead into the break when Kelleher, starting at hooker with captain Dan Sheehan playing at number eight for the first time, powered over from a smart lineout maul five yards out from the Springbok line.  South Africa started the second half a little better and Canan Moodie, an early replacement for the injured Damian Willemse, was a stray boot from a brilliant finish in the corner. But they could not get any kind of flow into their game, even after the deployment of their 'Bomb Squad' from the bench helped lead to the converted Marx try that set up the tight finish. Ireland crucially remained on the front foot and stood up to some late pressure to the dismay of Erasmus, who smashed the table at full time and shouted at a TV during a live online watch party he was hosting four kilometres away at the team hotel. "We never promise we're going to win every game, but we know as a group that we can definitely be better," said South Africa captain Siya Kolisi. "I don't question the boys' effort, I don't question their mindset and wanting to win all the time but it's just finding plans to be better and executing better... There's a lot that we know that we need to fix, but we do know how to fix it."

Source: Reuters

Nov 21 : World chess governing body FIDE referred Magnus Carlsen to its Ethics and Disciplinary Commission (EDC) after the Norwegian forfeited three games during a pilot event for the Total Chess World Championship Tour in Budapest, the federation said on Saturday. In a statement, FIDE criticised Carlsen for missing three scheduled games against Vladislav Artemiev while their 17th-place playoff was still undecided. Carlsen forfeited both rapid games on the opening day of the match and a fast classic game on day two before prevailing in an armageddon tie-break. “Given GM Carlsen’s stature and his significant role in promoting chess, such actions are particularly concerning, as they may damage the reputation of competitions and demonstrate a lack of respect for opponents, spectators, and tournament partners,” FIDE said.

Carlsen's rating and world number one ranking were under pressure during the tournament, with losses threatening to push him below the 2800 mark for the first time in 17 years and potentially end his more than 15-year reign at the top of the rankings. FIDE noted that other players also forfeited games in already-decided matches, but drew a distinction with Carlsen's absences against Artemiev while the result remained in doubt. The Budapest event, won by Alireza Firouzja ahead of Anish Giri and Fabiano Caruana, served as a test tournament for the inaugural Total Chess World Tour season in 2027.
